items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I would spend day after day, after day with Pepper Adams. Pepper Adams became my musical guru.

ctx.x: So, the Bluebird in is a place that is often…but it seems like there was an Eastside and a Westside thing happening in Detroit, and how did you fit into all of that?

Yes, there was. I was with the Westside guys. I was with Tommy Flanagan, Kenny Burrell, Pepper Adams, and before me the group was Frank Rosolino’s group. He left to go with Stan Kenton. Kenny Burrell grabbed me and put me in that because I was a Westside guy. Those guys were down there in the valley. They were way downtown and in primarily black schools, high schools and stuff. They were eastside kids, like the movies.
What was the club scene on the eastside like?

items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee discusses the 'Jones boys' (Elvin, Thad, Pepper) in the context of the interviewer's prompt and describes their musical styles and the local jazz scene, but does not describe a direct personal or professional relationship with the group as a whole or its members individually in this

ctx.x: Next to it or something, someplace near Detroit.

Yeah, I knew it but… Pontiac. The Jones boys were from Flint or someplace. Flint, Michigan -- all wear those car companies were was where, you know… There was so much talent there, there were so many musicians there, white and black. Half of the guys from… The drummer, the real hip drummer from Woody Herman’s band? He was a big-time drummer, Kenny Burrell used to play with him a lot. Frank Rosolino used to use him a lot.

items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When I went to Pepper Adams house... His best bud was not me, it was Elvin Jones.

ctx.x: Yeah, but he came out early.

So, he was allowed to go over there but I got off the bus once and they told me, "Get on the bus and go back where you came from.” So, I had to take my lessons from Elmer James at the music hall in downtown Detroit. I wasn't allowed in one part of downtown Detroit. I wasn't allowed to go out there. In fact, when I went to Pepper Adams house, a couple times I had to go into the trunk of the car during the day. I couldn't be seen riding in town with him. When I went into the service my two best friends, one of…
So did the pepperoni come from… Did the Park to the Pepper… To the pepperoni…is that…
